subject: Contract amendment — add EU & APAC reserved pools, throughput guarantees and failover
messages:
From: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@sofia-tech.com>

Cc: SofiaTech Procurement <contracts@sofia-tech.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:12:50 -0800
Subject: Q3 renewal + geo expansion request — EU & APAC pools

Hi Ben,

We're preparing our Q3 contract renewal and we want to add dedicated capacity in both EU and APAC to improve latency for EU and APAC users. Current commit: 20 reserved GPUs (US). We're proposing the following as part of the renewal: 

- EU: 8 reserved GPUs (same instance type as current pool)
- APAC: 6 reserved GPUs
- Throughput expectation: sustained 300 requests/sec per region during business hours (peak planning)
- Target p99 latency: <150ms for EU, <180ms for APAC (from regional clients)
- Failover behavior: automatic failover to US pool if regional pool is degraded; we need an RTO target and any added latency estimates for that path

We also want to extend the term to 12 months starting on contract signature. Please send an amendment/quote and any notes on how failover and KV/prefix caching will work cross-region.

Attached: usage snapshot and daily 95/99 latency samples for Jan–Mar.

Thanks,
Emily

Subject: RE: Q3 renewal + geo expansion request — technical note

Team — high level tech notes for the amendment: 

- Topology: we'll provision two isolated reserved pools (EU, APAC) with dedicated KV-cache per region to maintain local prefix cache hit rates. Cross-region KV fallback will be read-through only; we avoid cross-region write-sync to prevent consistency penalties.
- Throughput: an 8-GPU EU pool should sustain ~320 req/s with 90% cache hit; a 6-GPU APAC pool ~240 req/s. For 300 req/s sustained, we recommend configuring autoscaling headroom/burst capacity + a small dedicated burst reserve in each region (2 extra nodes) for 95th percentile traffic spikes.
- Latency (p99 realistic targets): EU p99 <= 200ms, APAC p99 <= 220ms with current model weights and 2048 token horizon. Achieving <150ms p99 in EU would require additional memory-optimized instances (cost delta TBD).
- Failover: when regional pool is degraded, traffic will be routed to US pool by our smart router. Expect added networking/runtime delta typically 200–350ms to p99 depending on client origin; we can include a failover SLO of RTO <= 5 minutes for routing convergence and an SLO that states failover-induced latency may exceed baseline.
- Guarantees: propose throughput guarantee clause (sustained 300 req/s) tied to a tokenized measurement window and a 95% availability target for the reserved pools. Credits for missed throughput/latency measured against agreed prompt set.

I'll add a short appendix with recommended node sizing and a simulated latency table.

Karthik
Head of Infrastructure Delivery
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency_modeling_notes.md]
